description:
WWW::Form::UrlEncoded::XS versions before 0.28 for Perl write past the end of the Perl argument stack when parse_urlencoded returns many pairs.

parse_urlencoded returns its result as a list, pushing each decoded key and value onto the argument stack without first extending the stack to fit them. parse_urlencoded_arrayref returns an array reference and is not affected.

A remote client that sends a query string or request body with many pairs to an application parsing it with parse_urlencoded can corrupt memory and crash the process.

Plane is an open-source project management tool. In versions prior to 1.4.0, the v2 asset static endpoint allows unauthenticated requests and returns presigned S3 URLs for an asset with access-signed parameters. Any user who knows an asset UUID can retrieve the signed URL without an account, providing access to that asset. This issue is fixed in version 1.4.0.

WWW::Form::UrlEncoded::XS versions before 0.27 for Perl read one byte before the input buffer when parsing an empty string.

parse_urlencoded and parse_urlencoded_arrayref check for a trailing "&" or ";" by reading the last byte of the input, without first checking that the input has any bytes.

A remote client that sends an empty query string or request body to an application parsing it with this module can crash the process.

PDF::API2 versions before 2.049 for Perl allow unbounded recursion via circular cross-reference chains in readxrtr.

When a PDF is opened, readxrtr reads each cross-reference table and calls itself on the offset in the trailer's /Prev entry. Nothing records which offsets it has already read, so a /Prev entry pointing back to an earlier table, or to its own, makes it recurse without end.

An attacker who supplies a crafted PDF can cause a denial of service in any application that opens it.

A flaw has been found in GL.iNet GL-A1300, GL-AR300M, GL-AR300M16, GL-AX1800, GL-AXT1800, GL-B3000, GL-BE3600, GL-BE6500, GL-BE9300, GL-BE10000, GL-BE14000, GL-E750, GL-E750V2, GL-E5800, GL-MT300N-V2, GL-MT1300, GL-MT2500, GL-MT2500A, GL-MT3000, GL-MT3600BE, GL-MT5000, GL-MT6000, GL-SFT1200, GL-X300B, GL-X750, GL-X750V2, GL-X2000, GL-X3000, GL-XE300 and GL-XE3000. The impacted element is the function ovpn-client.add_group of the file /rpc of the component Management RPC. Executing a manipulation can lead to null pointer dereference. The attack may be launched remotely. The affected component should be upgraded. This CVE was requested by the vendor.

Crypt::JWT versions before 0.024 for Perl skip issuer, subject, audience and JWT ID checks when the claim is absent or the option is a plain string.

decode_jwt runs the verify_iss, verify_sub, verify_aud and verify_jti checks only when the token carries the claim, and honours an option only as a Regexp or CODE reference. Any other value, such as verify_aud => 'myapp', is ignored.

An application that relies on these checks accepts a validly signed token meant for a different issuer, subject or audience.

Missing integrity verification vulnerabilities exist in the command line interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave) that could be exploited by a low-privileged local attacker if certain preconditions outside of the attacker's control are met. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to modify certain system data.

A weak cryptography vulnerability exists in HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an authenticated remote attacker with high privileges to obtain sensitive information from the affected system if certain preconditions outside of the attacker's control are met.

A vulnerability in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave) could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to conduct a reflected cross-site scripting (XSS) attack against a user of the interface. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary script code in a victim's browser in the context of the web interface.

Missing authorization vulnerabilities exist in the API of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an authenticated attacker with low privileges to modify data on the affected system.

An XML external entity (XXE) vulnerability exists in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an authenticated remote attacker with low privileges to obtain sensitive information from the affected system.

Path traversal vulnerabilities exist in the web-based management interface and API of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave), which could be exploited by an authenticated attacker with low privileges. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to read certain files on the underlying operating system.

Improper certificate validation vulnerabilities in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave) allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to circumvent existing authentication controls if certain preconditions outside of the attacker's control are met. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to gain administrative access to the affected system.

A command injection vulnerability exists in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an authenticated remote attacker with low privileges to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system if certain preconditions outside of the attacker's control are met.

A sensitive information disclosure vulnerability exists in the affected interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to obtain sensitive information from the affected system.

A missing integrity verification vulnerability exists in HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow a low-privileged local attacker to modify trusted system data on the affected system.

Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl allow memory exhaustion via unbounded inflation of zip DEF payloads.

When a token header sets "zip" to "DEF", decode_jwt inflates the payload with no limit on the output size. A signed token is inflated after its signature verifies. An encrypted token is inflated after decryption, and with RSA-OAEP or ECDH-ES key management anyone who holds the recipient's public key can produce a token that decrypts.

Authenticated SQL injection vulnerabilities in the web-based management interface and API of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave) could allow a low-privileged authenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary SQL statements against HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to obtain sensitive information from and modify data on the affected system.

A vulnerability in a system functionality could allow a low-privilege authenticated attacker with network access to potentially authenticate as an unintended user. Successful exploitation could allow an attacker to gain unauthorized access, potentially affecting system integrity, exposing sensitive information, or disrupting management operations.

A command injection vulnerability exists in the web-based management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying operating system of the affected system, impacting the confidentiality, integrity and availability of HPE Networking Management Software (AirWave).

A vulnerability in system functionality could allow an attacker with network access to bypass authentication. Successful exploitation could potentially allow an attacker to perform unauthorized actions, affecting system integrity and confidentiality.

An authentication bypass vulnerability exists in the web management interface of HPE Networking Management Software (Airwave). Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to gain unauthorized administrative access to the affected system, impacting the confidentiality and integrity of AirWave.

Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl allow CPU exhaustion via an unbounded PBES2 iteration count.

For a token using a PBES2 key management algorithm, decode_jwt passes the p2c header parameter to PBKDF2 as the iteration count without a range check, and derives the key before any integrity check. Unless accepted_alg rules it out, a token can select PBES2 whenever decode_jwt is given a symmetric key.

Crypt::JWT versions before 0.037_1 for Perl compare HMAC signatures and JWE authentication tags in non-constant time.

decode_jwt compares HS256, HS384 and HS512 signatures, and the authentication tag of A128CBC-HS256, A192CBC-HS384 and A256CBC-HS512 encrypted tokens, against the computed value with Perl's eq operator. Its run time depends on the number of matching leading bytes.

An attacker who can submit many candidate tokens and measure the timing precisely enough may recover the expected signature or tag byte by byte and forge a token that verifies.

psqlODBC rewrites statement text for keyset-driven cursors and ODBC escapes using positions it found in the text. These positions could lie outside the text or describe another statement:

- After SQLExecDirect() failed on a statement handle, the FROM and WHERE positions of the failed statement were applied to the next, shorter statement on that handle.
- The parser could record a FROM position with no text after it, and the rewrite then copied a negative length.
- An {fn …} escape whose arguments contain FOR UPDATE, ; or INTO … FROM made the driver remove a cursor prefix from the wrong buffer.
- {fn CONVERT(?, …)} with an output parameter produced a negative argument length.
- An unclosed {fn …} escape made the driver read past the statement, and a few thousand nested ones exhausted the stack.
- Translating @@identity in long statement text read an uninitialised pointer, and {? = call …} with nothing bound for the return value dereferenced NULL.

Whoever supplies the text of a statement that an application opens on a keyset-driven or dynamic cursor with a concurrency other than read-only, or calls with an output parameter, can corrupt the application's heap and end it. That includes the users of query tools, report builders and other applications that run SQL their users type. Code execution has not been demonstrated.

Versions up to and including psqlODBC 18.00.0006 are affected.
